text:
Allergies:
Patient recorded as having No Known Allergies to Drugs

Chief Complaint:
Acute Pancreatitis, Choledocolithiasis, Probable Cholangitis, 
Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response

History of Present Illness:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old gentleman normally cared for at the 
___, who is transferred from ___ for 
concern of acute cholangitis, pancreatitis, probable 
cholecystitis.

The patient began having pain in his abdomen while he was 
driving his car on the day prior to admission. He denies similar 
pain in the past. He reports yellow, non-bloody emesis but is 
unable to provide further details. He denies fevers, chills, 
chest pain, difficulty breathing, bloody, or black stools. He 
had a brown bowel movement on the morning his symptoms began. He 
was evaluated at ___ where a CT of his abdomen raised 
concern for biliary obstruction. He was therefore transferred to 
___ for possible ERCP.  
 
In the ___ ED, his vital signs were: Tm 99.4 79 199/76 18 95%. 
On exam, he was tender in his right upper quandrant but he did 
not have ___ sign. He underwent RUQ ultrasound, which 
revealed a dilated common bile duct at 1.4cm with mild 
intrahepatic ductal dilation. No definite CBD stone was seen, 
but there was sludge in the gall bladder. A CT abdomen was 
concerning for acute cholecystitis. The patient was seen by both 
surgery and ERCP, and the decision was made to pursue ERCP and 
reassess the patient after ERCP to determine whether he would 
need cholecystectomy. He was given 3L of IV fluids and started 
on unasyn before being admitted to the ICU for further care.  

Upon arrival in the ICU, he was sleepy and somewhat disoriented. 
He initially denied any abdominal pain, then pointed to his 
epigastric area saying it had been hurting all day and continued 
to hurt. He then denied pain again. His greatest concern was 
that he was very thirsty. He denied back pain or headache.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old gentleman with CAD, HTN, and DM presenting with RUQ 
pain and obstructive LFTs concerning for cholangitis.  

1. Acute Cholecystitis, Acute Pancreatitis, Acute Cholangitis, 
Choledocolithiasis:  Probable gallstone pancreatitis at OSH. 
Imaging also suggested coincident cholecystitis. He was placed 
on IV unasyn for cholangitis and admitted to the ICU for closer 
monitoring due to concern for sepsis. While in the ICU, the 
patient did not require any pressors and received ___ of IVFs 
overnight for fluid resuscitation in addition to the fluid 
received in the ED. He was seen by the ERCP team and had a ERCP 
where pus appearing bile was seen in a dilated CBD, stent 
deployed, and sphincterotomy was performed with good flow of 
purulent bile noted post stent placement. Multiple stone ranging 
from 4-6 mm were seen in the CBD. Surgery was also consulted for 
question of need for cholecystectomy, which they recommended be 
performed during this hospitalization. Due to the patient's 
preference to have the procedure performed closer to home at the 
___, the surgeons deferred management of CCY 
until the patient can be transferred to the OSH. Blood cultures 
revealed no growth to date by the time of transfer to the 
medical floor. His LFTs also normalized by the time of transfer 
to the medical floor. Pt was initially on Unasyn but that was 
switched to oral ciprofloxacin and flagyl to finish a 10 day 
course for possible cholangitis. As a bed was not available at 
the ___, the patient requested transfer to ___ 
___, and he was accepted by Dr. ___.

2. Fevers:
Likely due to biliary and gallbladder processes as above. Blood 
and urine cultures no growth. He was noted to have a cough on 
exam, and although the patient reported this was a chronic cough 
and likely secondary to bronchitis due to his long smoking 
history, a sputum culture was sent that revealed no 
microorganisms on gram stain, sparse OP flora, and rare GNRs. 
Given there was no clear infiltrates on CXR and cough was 
unchanged per pt, he was not specifically treated for a PNA. A 
repeat CXR was done and it did not demonstrate a pneumonia.

3. Atrial fibrillation With rapid ventricular response:
Developed on hospital day 2. Per patient, this is a new 
diagnosis for him. Predisposing factors for atrial fibrillation 
include underlying infection and preexisting enlarged atria 
bilaterally. Heart Rate initially up to 140-150s but maintained 
hemodynamic stability and patient was completely assymptomatic. 
EKG revealed 1-___epressions in V2-5, consistent with rate 
related demand ischemia. Cardiac enzymes were cycled with CKs 
not elevated and troponin 0.03 from undetectable on admission. 
Aspirin was increased to 325 mg po daily. Given multiple rounds 
of IV lopressor and IV dilitazem with some improvement in HR to 
110s. PO beta-blocker was titrated up and digoxin loaded the 
following day with improvement in HR to 80-90s. He was not 
started on heparin gtt with bridge to coumadin as the patient 
reported that he had a severe peptic ulcer bleed ___ years ago 
while being on plavix and his PCP had told him that he should 
not receive any anti-coagulation in the future as well as 
upcoming surgery. He was also not deemed a cardioversion 
candidate as it was unclear if the patient was in atrial 
fibrillation chronically given the fact that he was completely 
assymptomatic while in atrial fibrillation. On the general 
floor, his resting heart rate was in 80-90s with occassional 
bursts into 140s; particularly w exertion and pt's bb was 
uptitrated as needed, with good result.

4. Benign Hypertension:
Although the patient was hypertensive upon arrival from the ED, 
his BP meds were initially held due to concern for possible 
developing sepsis. Due to persistently elevated BPs, he was 
starated on captopril 12.5 mg tid and eventually restarted on 
beta-blockers as well, which were titrated up to help with rate 
control (#3) to metoprolol 75mg bid and his home dose ACE-I was 
also restarted.

5. Acute Delerium:
He had one episode of agitation in ICU, likely secondary to 
sundowning in this elderly gentleman who has been to multiple 
hospitals and received IV narcotics initially for abdominal 
pain. ABG ruled out hypercarbia. During his ICU course, he 
progressively became more agitated as he wished to be 
transferred to the ___. Although it was 
explained to the patient that this could not happen given his 
current clinical status, he continued to escalate and received 
haldol and ativan with good effect. Frequent reorientation was 
also provided. On floor, although the patient kept demanding to 
want to go to the ___ he was not agitated, and with normal 
sleep/wake cycle was calm.

6. Type 2 DM Uncontrolled with Complications:
Held oral diabetic meds on admission and given upcoming surgery 
were not restarted on transfer. Started on HISS. 

7. CAD Bypass Vessle:
ASA increased to 325 mg daily given atrial fibrillation as 
above. B-blocker also titrated up for rate control as above. 
Statin initially held due to elevated LFTs. EKG while pt in afib 
with RVR revealed ST depressions in anteroseptal leads 
suggestive of rate related demand ischemia. Cardiac enzymes not 
suggestive of ACS.   

8. Peripheral Vascular Disease: 
Held cilostazol as non-formulary medication.

9. Question of thyroid nodule:
Per review of OSH records. ___ need follow-up as an outpt.

10. Tobacco Dependence, COPD: 
Counseled regarding tobacco cessation. Nicotine patch offered 
and continued on advair. Albuterol and Atrovent nebs.

11. Hyperlipidemia:
Not on problem list from OSH records, but on statin and 
gemfibrozil as an outpatient. Initially held simvastatin and 
gemfibrozil until LFTs improved. By the time of transfer to the 
floor, statin had been restarted and gemfibrozil remained held. 

12. BPH Without Obstruction:
Initially held terazosin, which was restarted by the time of 
transfer to the floor. He had not urinary retention. 

13. Anemia of chronic disease: 
Hematocrit monitored daily. Iron studies with ACD. Elevated 
ferritin c/w inflammatory state.

14. h/o Malignant Neoplasm - Prostate: 
Not active during this admission
